 ABRAHAM KURIAN PLAMTHOTTAM

 REENU ALIYAMMA CHERIAN, AGED 35 YEARS
 D/O DR. CHERIAN THOMAS, CHERADI HOUSE, ST. GEORGE LPS

 BY ADV SMT.ASHA BABU


 THIS MATRIMONIAL APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR HEARING ON
24.06.2026, THE COURT ON 30.06.2026 DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022

 2
 2026:KER:46426


 SATHISH NINAN & P. KRISHNA KUMAR, JJ.
 = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = =
 Mat.Appeal No.204 OF 2022
 = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = =
 Dated this the 30th day of June, 2026

 JUDGMENT
P.Krishna Kumar, J.

A petition filed under Section 10(ix) and (x) of the

 Divorce Act, 1869 ("the Act", for short), by the husband was

dismissed by the Family Court, Ettumanoor. Aggrieved thereby, the

husband has preferred this appeal.

2. The appellant married the respondent on 26.12.2011 in

accordance with Christian religious rites and ceremonies. The

appellant alleges that their matrimonial relationship completely

broke down on account of the cruel conduct of the respondent

towards him and his mother. According to him, the respondent made

false and scandalous allegations against him and his mother,

thereby subjecting him to cruelty. The appellant further alleges

that the respondent had been undergoing regular medical treatment

but never disclosed to him the actual nature of her illness.

According to the appellant, when he realised that the respondent

had been making false allegations against him and his mother, he

arranged several counselling sessions, which both parties
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 3
 2026:KER:46426

attended. However, all such attempts proved futile. It is also

alleged that the respondent deserted the appellant on 13.01.2013.

Accordingly, the appellant filed the petition for divorce, about

five years after the marriage.

3. The respondent resisted the petition by contending that

it was the appellant's mother who was responsible for all the

problems in their matrimonial life, though the respondent had

been leading the life of a devoted wife. According to the

respondent, she had been suffering from intermittent fever and

had undergone medical tests as prescribed by her father and by

the doctors at Indira Gandhi Co-operative Hospital, Kochi.

Although all the test results were normal, the doctors advised

her to avoid situations causing mental stress. The doctors at

Kochi wanted to discuss the matter with the appellant, but he

refused to come to Kochi. They advised the respondent to take up

employment in Kochi and to return to Bangalore, where the

appellant was residing, only after the existing family issues

were resolved, failing which her health would further

deteriorate. The respondent contends that she attended a job

interview with the consent of the appellant, but after she

received the appointment letter on 31.01.2013, the appellant

started avoiding her by not attending her calls. Feeling
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 4
 2026:KER:46426

abandoned by the appellant, she acted upon the advice of the

doctors as well as her family members and joined the employment

in Kochi. According to her, it was under these circumstances that

she started residing in Kochi and therefore, she cannot be

accused of having deserted the appellant. The respondent further

contends that, following mediation and counselling, she decided

to resign from her employment with Burndy Technology and Global

Business Services Pvt. Ltd. solely for the purpose of residing

with the appellant in Bangalore. In the above circumstances, the

respondent claims that she is the victim of the cruelty inflicted

by the appellant's mother and, therefore, the petition for

divorce is liable to be dismissed.

4. Upon evaluating the oral and documentary evidence adduced

during the trial, the Family Court concluded that there was no

evidence to establish either cruelty or desertion as alleged and,

accordingly, dismissed the petition.

5. We have heard Dr. Sebastian Champappilly, the learned

counsel appearing for the appellant, and Smt. Rexy Elizabeth

Thomas, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent.

6. Referring to the decisions in Rajib Kumar Roy v.

Sushmita Saha ( 2023 KHC 7090), Roopa Soni v. Kamalnarayan Soni 

( 2023 KHC 6828), Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan (2023 (3)
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 5
 2026:KER:46426

KHC 435), Beena M.S. v. Shino G. Babu (2022 (2) KHC 11), X v. Y

(2001 KHC 479), Shri Kumar V. Unnithan v. Manju K. Nair (2007 (4)

KHC 807), Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh ( 2007 (2) KHC 231) and K.

Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa (2013 (1) KHC 647), the learned

counsel for the appellant contended that the acts of the

respondent, which stand proved in the present case, clearly

constitute matrimonial cruelty within the meaning of Section 10 

of the Act and that the matrimonial bond has, for all practical

purposes, irretrievably broken down with no possibility of its

restoration.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the

respondent contended that none of the grounds urged by the

appellant has been established during the trial and that the

respondent has always been ready and willing to resume the

matrimonial relationship. It is further contended that the

respondent resigned from her employment solely with a view to

restoring the marital relationship, but the appellant's mother

prevented such reunion.

8. Considering the comparatively young age of the appellant

and the respondent and the repeated assertion made by the learned

counsel for the respondent that the respondent-wife was willing

to resume cohabitation, we thought it appropriate to interact
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 6
 2026:KER:46426

with both parties. However, the interaction did not instill in us

any confidence that there remains a realistic possibility of

reconciliation.

9. In the light of the rival contentions, the point that

arises for determination is whether the appellant is entitled to

a decree of divorce on the grounds of cruelty and desertion.

10. The appellant seeks a decree of divorce primarily on the

allegation that, from the very inception of the marriage, the

respondent showed no interest in leading a normal matrimonial

life as she was suffering from an illness or disease, the details

of which she never disclosed to him. It is further alleged that

the respondent caused him severe mental agony and hardship by her

various acts of cruelty.

11. On an overall appreciation of the evidence of PWs 1 and

2 vis-à-vis the evidence of RW1, we find some merit in the

contention advanced by the appellant. Even if several instances

relied on by the appellant to establish cruelty are treated as

mere wear and tear of matrimonial life, certain other incidents

cannot be viewed in the same light. It is the specific case of

the appellant that the respondent had suppressed from him the

true nature of her illness throughout their matrimonial life. His

grievance is that the respondent had been suffering from
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 7
 2026:KER:46426

recurring illness, which she consistently described as fever.

Significantly, while the parties were residing in Bangalore, the

respondent returned to Kochi and underwent medical treatment.

Admittedly, she had gone to Kochi to take up employment, but when

she ultimately joined a firm, she failed to inform the appellant.

She claims that she had attempted to inform the appellant, but he

did not answer her calls. She was compelled to take up employment

at Kochi on the advice of the doctors, and the predominant reason

for accepting employment away from the appellant was to avoid the

stressful circumstances arising out of their matrimonial life.

These facts are not in dispute. The relevant part of her proof

affidavit reads thus:

"17. The allegations that two days after my arrival in Kochi,
 I informed the petitioner that I joined in a company named
 'Hubbell Burndy' and having heard the same, he was shocked is
 incorrect. After reaching Kochi, I along with my mother
 consulted the doctor at the Indira Ganghi Co-operative
 hospital for my fever and various medical tests were also
 conducted. But since the entire test reports were found to be
 normal, the doctor advised me to refrain from events causing
 mental stress. As the doctor wanted to have a discussion on
 this with the petitioner, I conveyed the same to the
 petitioner over phone. But as the petitioner refused to come
 to Kochi, the doctor advised me to get engaged in some
 activities or to take up a job in Kochi. It is also advised
 by the doctor that it was better for me to go to Bangalore
 only after settling the existing family issues failing which
 it would cause more harm to my health. On 20.1.2013. I was
 asked to attend an interview for a job in Burndy Technology
 and Global Business services Pvt. Ltd.. The same was informed
 to the petitioner also by me over phone and he also suggested
 attending the interview. After a few rounds of interviews I
 got selected by the said company and I received the
 appointment letter only on 31.1.2013. (offer letter is
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 8
 2026:KER:46426

 produced). When I had to take a final decision on joining the
 job, I tried to contact the petitioner. But instead of giving
 a decision, petitioner started to avoid me by not attending
 my further phone calls. I was really taken by a surprise due
 to the sudden change in the behaviour of the petitioner. As I
 felt deserted by the petitioner, I had no option but to heed
 to the advice of the doctor and also my family members.
 Accordingly I had to join the said job. Hence the allegation
 that petitioner felt cheated and insulted and my acts caused
 humiliation and mental agony to the petitioner is totally
 incorrect."

12. According to the respondent, she was suffering from

intermittent fever, for which she had undergone treatment under

her father, a general physician, as well as two other doctors

attached to different hospitals. However, a close scrutiny of the

matters elicited in her cross-examination does not indicate that

she was merely suffering from an ordinary episode of fever. On

the contrary, her evidence suggests that she was reluctant to

disclose to her husband the true nature of the ailment for which

she was undergoing treatment. She even went to the extent of

stating that she was unaware that one of the grounds urged in the

divorce petition was her failure to disclose the true nature of

her illness and the medical tests she had undergone. She stated

as follows:

"Intermittent fever വവിവവാഹതവിനുമുമമ്പ് ഉണവായവിടവില. 13.5.12 നമ്പ് ശശേഷഷ
 കകവാചവിയവിൽ ഞവാൻ ആയവിരവിക്കുശമവാൾ ആണമ്പ് ആദദ്യമവായവി പവാരവാതവികവാരശനവാടമ്പ്
 എനവികമ്പ് പനവി ഉണമ്പ് എനമ്പ് പറയുനതമ്പ് എനമ്പ് പറഞവാൽ ശേരവിയല. എകന
 അച്ഛൻ, Dr.Sahib , Dr.Joseph Kurian എനവിവരുകട നവിർശദ്ദേശേപ്രകവാരഷ ആണമ്പ്
 test നടതവിയതമ്പ് . എകന അച്ഛൻ General medicine ൽ ആണമ്പ് specialise
 കചെയവിരുനതമ്പ് . അച്ഛൻ അനമ്പ് ഇനവിരവാഗവാനവിയുകട ആശുപതവിയവിൽ ആയവിരുന.
 Dr. Sahib Physician ആണമ്പ് . MAJ ആശുപതവി ഇടപ്പളവിയവിലവാണമ്പ്.

2026:KER:46426

 Joseph കുരദ്യൻ ഇനവിരവാഗവാനവി ശകവാപ്പശററവിവമ്പ് ആശുപതവിയവിൽ physician
 ആണമ്പ് . Blood test കൾ നടതവി. TB യുശടതമ്പ് H1N1 നടതവി. ഈ
 ശഡവാക്ടർമവാരുകട prescription നൽകവി. ആ prescription
 ഹവാജരവാകവാതവിരവികവാൻ കവാരണഷ ഉശണവാ (Q) ഈ ശകസവിൽ ആവശേദ്യമവില എനമ്പ്
 ശതവാനവി (A) അതുകകവാണവാണമ്പ് ശഡവാക്ടർമവാരുകട ശപരമ്പ് ആശക്ഷേപതവിൽ
 പറയവാതവിരുനതമ്പ്. 2013-ൽ ശജവാസഫമ്പ് കുരവിയൻ എന ശഡവാക്ടറവികന ആണമ്പ്
 കണതമ്പ്. ശവശറ ശഡവാക്ടർമവാകര കണവിരുന. Menstrual irregularities നമ്പ്
 ശവണവി ആണമ്പ് . അതമ്പ് Homeo doctor കന ആണമ്പ് കണതമ്പ്. അതമ്പ് ആലപ്പുഴ
 ആണമ്പ് . അതമ്പ് നവഷബർ 2012 ൽ ആണമ്പ് കണതമ്പ് . വവിവവാഹ ജജീവവിതതവിൽ
 പ്രശേനഷ ഉശണവാ എനമ്പ് ശഡവാക്ടർ ശജവാസഫമ്പ് കുരവിയൻ ആണമ്പ് ശചെവാദവിചതമ്പ് . Test-
 ൽ പ്രശ്നങ്ങൾ ഒനഷ കവാണവാകത വനശപ്പവാൾ stress മൂലഷ ആശണവാ എനമ്പ്
 അറവിയവാൻ ശവണവിയവാണമ്പ് അങ്ങകന ശചെവാദവിചതമ്പ് . അമവായവിഅമ പ്രശ്നങ്ങൾ
 ഉണവാക്കുനണമ്പ് എനമ്പ് പറഞവിരുന. Chief affidavit 13)o ഖണവികയവിൽ I
 had allowed the petitioner to contact that doctor എന പറഞവിട്ടുളതമ്പ്
 ശഹവാമവിശയവാ ശഡവാക്ടറവികനയവാണമ്പ്. 2012 ഡവിസഷബറവിൽ ആണമ്പ് ഭർതവാവവിശനവാടമ്പ്
 menstrual irregularities ഉണമ്പ് എന കവാരദ്യഷ പറഞതമ്പ്. ഞവാൻ 2012
 ഡവിസഷബറവിൽ കചെനതവിനു ശശേഷഷ ശഹവാമവിശയവാമരുനഷ, ഇഷഗമ്പ്ളജീഷമ്പ് മരുനഷ
 കഴവിക്കുനണവായവിരുന എനമ്പ് പറഞവാൽ ശഹവാമവിശയവാമരുനമവാതഷ. ശഹവാമവിശയവാ
 മരുനമ്പ് കഴവിഞ്ഞു എനഷ അതുവവാങ്ങണഷ എനപറഞവാണമ്പ് ഞവാൻ വജീടവിൽ
 ശപവാകണഷ എന പറഞതമ്പ് എന പറഞവാൽ ഞവാൻ ആവശേദ്യകപ്പടവിടവില.
 Intermittent fever നമ്പ് stress ആണമ്പ് കവാരണഷ എനവാണമ്പ് ശഡവാക്ടർ
 കണ്ടുപവിടവിചതമ്പ്. അതമ്പ് ഒരു condition ആണമ്പ് എനവാണമ്പ് പറഞതമ്പ് . It is
 called essential hyper thermia. അതവിനമ്പ് മരുനമ്പ് കഴവിചവില. Clonazempama
 menstrual irregularity കമ്പ് നവിങ്ങൾ കഴവിചതവാശണവാ (Q) ഞവാൻ കഴവിചവിടവില
 (A) എകന അസുഖതവികനപ്പറവിശയവാ ഞവാൻ നടതവിയ test കന പറവിശയവാ ഞവാൻ
 എകന ഭർതവാവവിശനവാടു നവാളവിതുവകര കവളവികപ്പടുതവിയവിടവില എനമ്പ് പറഞവാൽ
 കവളവികപ്പടുതവിയവിരുന. അങ്ങവികന കവളവികപ്പടുതൽ ഈ ഹർജവിയവികല divorce

-ൽ ഒരു ground ആയവി ഭർതവാവു പറഞതവായവി നവിങ്ങൾകമ്പ് മനസവിലവാശയവാ
 (Q) മനസവിലവായവിടവില (A) എനവികമ്പ് ഭർതവാവവിശനവാടമ്പ് കവളവികപ്പടുതവാൻ
 പറവാത തരതവിലുള illness / disease എനവിക്കുണമ്പ്' എനമ്പ് ഹർജവികവാരൻ
 പറയുന എന പറഞവാൽ അതമ്പ് കതറവാണമ്പ് . അങ്ങവികന അസുഖഷ ഉളതമ്പ്
 കകവാണവാണമ്പ് ശഡവാക്ടർമവാരുകട വവിവരവുഷ ചെവികവിതവാവവിവരങ്ങളഷ മറഷ
 കവളവികപ്പടുതവാതവിരുനതമ്പ് എനഷ ശരഖകൾ ഹവാജരവാകവാതതുഷ എനമ്പ്
 പറഞവാൽ കതറവാണമ്പ്. അതമ്പ് ഞവാൻ കവാണവിച കവാരദ്യങ്ങളവാണമ്പ്. 2012 ജൂലവായവിൽ
 എകന അസുഖതവികന വവിവരങ്ങൾ അറവിയവാൻ അനമ്പ് എകന ഭർതവാവമ്പ് എകന
 അച്ഛകന വവിളവിചശപ്പവാൾ നവാടവിൽ ഉടകന വരണകമന ആവശേദ്യകപ്പടമ്പ് എന
 പറഞവാൽ ഭർതവാവമ്പ് വവിളവിചശപ്പവാൾ അച്ഛൻ വരണകമന പറഞ്ഞു."

The above circumstances clearly reveal that the respondent had

been under the care of three doctors, including her father, who

is a Doctor. Despite undergoing various medical examinations at

different hospitals, the doctors could not ascertain the cause of

her ailment, except to attribute it to mental stress. It is also
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 10
 2026:KER:46426

evident that she was advised to take up employment at her native

place, away from Bangalore where the appellant was residing.

Equally significant is the fact that the respondent was unable to

communicate to the appellant her decision to accept the

employment at a far away place.

13. The circumstances emerging from the cross-examination of

RW1 render the appellant's case highly probable that he was kept

in the dark regarding the nature of the respondent's illness, the

treatment administered to her, and the diagnosis made by the

doctors. In the above factual backdrop, the appellant's

contention that the respondent deserted him on 13.01.2013 also

appears to be probable.

14. Another circumstance emerging from the evidence is the

inference that can be drawn from the email communications

exchanged between the parties. Ext. A3 e-mail was sent by the

appellant on 27.07.2012 at 7.33 p.m., and there is no dispute

regarding its receipt by the respondent. In the said

communication, the appellant expressed his anguish that there was

a wide gap between the respondent's words and her conduct and

that he was exhausted by what he perceived to be her repeated
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 11
 2026:KER:46426

falsehoods and insincere explanations. He also narrated the

circumstances which, according to him, had resulted in a complete

erosion of trust between them. Though the e-mail was sent by the

appellant, it was generated much before the initiation of the

legal proceedings and hence it has some relevance.

15. On an overall evaluation of the evidence adduced by both

sides and in the light of the above materials, we find the case

put forward by the appellant to be more probable and acceptable

than the version of the respondent. The circumstances referred to

above sufficiently justify the appellant's apprehension that

continuation of the matrimonial relationship with the respondent

would be detrimental to his mental well-being. The evidence also

indicates that the respondent has been living separately from the

appellant since 13.01.2013. Although the respondent has

consistently contended that she was always ready and willing to

resume cohabitation, she did not initiate any proceedings for

restitution of conjugal rights.

16. In Shaji Sebastian v. Julie Joseph (2026 (1) KHC 523),

this Court observed that the expression "cruelty" occurring in

 Section 10(ix) of the Act cannot be assigned a different standard
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 12
 2026:KER:46426

from that applicable to the similar expression employed in other

matrimonial statutes. It is settled that where the mental cruelty

suffered by one spouse is of such a degree that the parties

cannot reasonably be expected to live together, a decree of

divorce may be granted ( Shri Kumar V. Unnithan v. Manju K. Nair

(supra)). Whether a particular conduct amounts to cruelty depends

upon the facts and circumstances of each case, including the

social status, educational background and professional standing

of the parties. What constitutes cruelty in one case may not

necessarily amount to cruelty in another, it is held.

17. In view of the facts discussed above, we find

that the appellant is entitled to get the relief of divorce on

the ground of cruelty and desertion.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by setting aside the

impugned decree and judgment. The marriage between the appellant

and the respondent is dissolved by a decree of divorce under

 Section 10 (ix) and (x) of the Divorce Act .
Sd/-

SATHISH NINAN, JUDGE

[p_1] P.Krishna Kumar, J.

[p_2] A petition filed under Section 10(ix) and (x) of the

 Divorce Act, 1869 ("the Act", for short), by the husband was

dismissed by the Family Court, Ettumanoor. Aggrieved thereby, the

husband has preferred this appeal.

[p_3] 2. The appellant married the respondent on 26.12.2011 in

accordance with Christian religious rites and ceremonies. The

appellant alleges that their matrimonial relationship completely

broke down on account of the cruel conduct of the respondent

towards him and his mother. According to him, the respondent made

false and scandalous allegations against him and his mother,

thereby subjecting him to cruelty. The appellant further alleges

that the respondent had been undergoing regular medical treatment

but never disclosed to him the actual nature of her illness.

According to the appellant, when he realised that the respondent

had been making false allegations against him and his mother, he

arranged several counselling sessions, which both parties
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 3
 2026:KER:46426

attended. However, all such attempts proved futile. It is also

alleged that the respondent deserted the appellant on 13.01.2013.

Accordingly, the appellant filed the petition for divorce, about

five years after the marriage.

[p_4] 3. The respondent resisted the petition by contending that

it was the appellant's mother who was responsible for all the

problems in their matrimonial life, though the respondent had

been leading the life of a devoted wife. According to the

respondent, she had been suffering from intermittent fever and

had undergone medical tests as prescribed by her father and by

the doctors at Indira Gandhi Co-operative Hospital, Kochi.

Although all the test results were normal, the doctors advised

her to avoid situations causing mental stress. The doctors at

Kochi wanted to discuss the matter with the appellant, but he

refused to come to Kochi. They advised the respondent to take up

employment in Kochi and to return to Bangalore, where the

appellant was residing, only after the existing family issues

were resolved, failing which her health would further

deteriorate. The respondent contends that she attended a job

interview with the consent of the appellant, but after she

received the appointment letter on 31.01.2013, the appellant

started avoiding her by not attending her calls. Feeling

abandoned by the appellant, she acted upon the advice of the

accused of having deserted the appellant. The respondent further

contends that, following mediation and counselling, she decided

to resign from her employment with Burndy Technology and Global

Business Services Pvt. Ltd. solely for the purpose of residing

with the appellant in Bangalore. In the above circumstances, the

respondent claims that she is the victim of the cruelty inflicted

by the appellant's mother and, therefore, the petition for

divorce is liable to be dismissed.

[p_5] 4. Upon evaluating the oral and documentary evidence adduced

during the trial, the Family Court concluded that there was no

evidence to establish either cruelty or desertion as alleged and,

accordingly, dismissed the petition.

[p_6] 5. We have heard Dr. Sebastian Champappilly, the learned

Thomas, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent.

[p_7] 6. Referring to the decisions in Rajib Kumar Roy v.

Sushmita Saha ( 2023 KHC 7090), Roopa Soni v. Kamalnarayan Soni

KHC 807), Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh ( 2007 (2) KHC 231) and K.

Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa (2013 (1) KHC 647), the learned

counsel for the appellant contended that the acts of the

respondent, which stand proved in the present case, clearly

of the Act and that the matrimonial bond has, for all practical

[p_8] 7. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the

respondent contended that none of the grounds urged by the

appellant has been established during the trial and that the

respondent has always been ready and willing to resume the

matrimonial relationship. It is further contended that the

respondent resigned from her employment solely with a view to

restoring the marital relationship, but the appellant's mother

prevented such reunion.

[p_9] 8. Considering the comparatively young age of the appellant

and the respondent and the repeated assertion made by the learned

counsel for the respondent that the respondent-wife was willing

to resume cohabitation, we thought it appropriate to interact

[p_10] 9. In the light of the rival contentions, the point that

a decree of divorce on the grounds of cruelty and desertion.

[p_11] 10. The appellant seeks a decree of divorce primarily on the

allegation that, from the very inception of the marriage, the

respondent showed no interest in leading a normal matrimonial

life as she was suffering from an illness or disease, the details

[p_12] 11. On an overall appreciation of the evidence of PWs 1 and

 പറഞവാൽ ഭർതവാവമ്പ് വവിളവിചശപ്പവാൾ അച്ഛൻ വരണകമന പറഞ്ഞു."

[p_14] The above circumstances clearly reveal that the respondent had

been under the care of three doctors, including her father, who

is a Doctor. Despite undergoing various medical examinations at

different hospitals, the doctors could not ascertain the cause of

her ailment, except to attribute it to mental stress. It is also
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 10
 2026:KER:46426

evident that she was advised to take up employment at her native

place, away from Bangalore where the appellant was residing.

Equally significant is the fact that the respondent was unable to

communicate to the appellant her decision to accept the

employment at a far away place.

[p_16] 13. The circumstances emerging from the cross-examination of

RW1 render the appellant's case highly probable that he was kept

in the dark regarding the nature of the respondent's illness, the

treatment administered to her, and the diagnosis made by the

doctors. In the above factual backdrop, the appellant's

contention that the respondent deserted him on 13.01.2013 also

appears to be probable.

[p_18] 14. Another circumstance emerging from the evidence is the

inference that can be drawn from the email communications

exchanged between the parties. Ext. A3 e-mail was sent by the

appellant on 27.07.2012 at 7.33 p.m., and there is no dispute

regarding its receipt by the respondent. In the said

communication, the appellant expressed his anguish that there was

a wide gap between the respondent's words and her conduct and

that he was exhausted by what he perceived to be her repeated
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 11
 2026:KER:46426

falsehoods and insincere explanations. He also narrated the

circumstances which, according to him, had resulted in a complete

erosion of trust between them. Though the e-mail was sent by the

appellant, it was generated much before the initiation of the

legal proceedings and hence it has some relevance.

[p_19] 15. On an overall evaluation of the evidence adduced by both

sides and in the light of the above materials, we find the case

put forward by the appellant to be more probable and acceptable

than the version of the respondent. The circumstances referred to

above sufficiently justify the appellant's apprehension that

continuation of the matrimonial relationship with the respondent

would be detrimental to his mental well-being. The evidence also

indicates that the respondent has been living separately from the

appellant since 13.01.2013. Although the respondent has

consistently contended that she was always ready and willing to

resume cohabitation, she did not initiate any proceedings for

restitution of conjugal rights.

[p_21] 16. In Shaji Sebastian v. Julie Joseph (2026 (1) KHC 523),

this Court observed that the expression "cruelty" occurring in

 Section 10(ix) of the Act cannot be assigned a different standard
 Mat.Appeal No.204/2022
 12
 2026:KER:46426

from that applicable to the similar expression employed in other

matrimonial statutes. It is settled that where the mental cruelty

suffered by one spouse is of such a degree that the parties

cannot reasonably be expected to live together, a decree of

divorce may be granted ( Shri Kumar V. Unnithan v. Manju K. Nair

(supra)). Whether a particular conduct amounts to cruelty depends

upon the facts and circumstances of each case, including the

social status, educational background and professional standing

of the parties. What constitutes cruelty in one case may not

necessarily amount to cruelty in another, it is held.

[p_22] 17. In view of the facts discussed above, we find

that the appellant is entitled to get the relief of divorce on

the ground of cruelty and desertion.

[p_23] In the result, the appeal is allowed by setting aside the

impugned decree and judgment. The marriage between the appellant

and the respondent is dissolved by a decree of divorce under

 Section 10 (ix) and (x) of the Divorce Act .
